title: Lesson 3: Prayer
description: Prayer is a child talking with a Father who loves to listen. This lesson walks through the six-step pattern Jesus gave in the Lord's Prayer and helps you build your own daily prayers.

blocks.text: In the last lesson you saw that God gave you new life and adopted you into His family. Children talk with their father. That is what prayer is, and in this lesson you will learn the pattern Jesus gave for it.

blocks.title: Teach Us to Pray
blocks.text:
The disciples watched Jesus pray. He got up while it was still dark and went to quiet places to talk with His Father (Mark 1:35). Before He chose the twelve, He prayed all night (Luke 6:12). Prayer was not a duty He squeezed in. It was the air He breathed.

One day, when He finished praying, one of His disciples asked Him for help: "Lord, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples" (Luke 11:1).

They did not ask Jesus how to preach or how to do miracles. They asked Him how to pray. And the very first word He gave them was Father (Luke 11:2).
What is Prayer?

Even the disciples had to learn to pray, so you can too. Prayer is a conversation: talking with and listening to God. Prayer displays our dependence on a powerful and loving Father. Because of Jesus, you do not come to God as a stranger hoping He will notice you. You come as His child. Prayer is a child talking with a Father who loves to listen.
For you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, "Abba! Father!"
3.1 - How would you describe your prayer life right now?
The Pattern Jesus Gave

Jesus taught us to pray in the Lord's Prayer, giving us a pattern to follow. Read the prayer below. This is the familiar wording many Christians pray, and it is the same wording the Daily Prayers tool uses at the end of this lesson. You can read Jesus' words for yourself in Matthew 6:9-13.

blocks.reference: The Lord's Prayer (traditional wording, from Matthew 6:9-13)
blocks.text:
Our Father, who is in heaven,
Holy is your name,
your kingdom come, your will be done
on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us this day our daily bread.
Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us.
And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
For yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory forever, Amen.
The prayer moves in six simple steps. You do not have to pray them perfectly or word for word. Think of them as six rooms you walk through with your Father.
STEP 1 - CONNECT RELATIONALLY
"Our Father, who is in heaven"
God has adopted us as His children and loves for us to call Him our Father. Starting prayer by acknowledging our relationship with God is powerful for us and delights Him.
3.2 - Why is it important to begin your prayers being reminded that God is your Father?
STEP 2 - WORSHIP HIS NAME
"Holy is your name"

When we proclaim who He is, we worship Him by reminding ourselves how powerful and great our God is. He is love, grace, and forgiveness. Try naming one thing that is true about Him: He is faithful, He is holy, He is near.
STEP 3 - PRAY HIS AGENDA FIRST
"your kingdom come, your will be done on earth as it is in heaven"
Part of being a child of God is caring about what He cares about. We acknowledge His wisdom and sovereignty when we pray His agenda first.
3.3 - What are some things that God cares about that you could pray about?
STEP 4 - DEPEND ON HIM FOR EVERYTHING
"Give us this day our daily bread."
God promises to supply all our needs. He wants us to come to Him with our problems, needs, and desires and to trust Him to provide.
3.4 - What are some of your current needs that you want God to provide for?
STEP 5 - FORGIVE AND BE FORGIVEN
"Forgive us our sins, as we forgive those who sin against us."
Through Jesus, God has offered us complete forgiveness. When we receive His forgiveness, our hearts are more prepared to forgive others as well.
STEP 6 - ENGAGE IN SPIRITUAL WARFARE
"And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil."
We have an enemy trying to steal, kill, and destroy. As we pray, we take our stand against the enemy and fight from victory through Jesus.
3.5 - What temptation or spiritual battle do you need God's help with right now?
This Week's Practice

You just walked through the six steps of the Lord's Prayer. Now it is time to make it personal. We built a tool that helps you take what you just learned and turn it into your own daily prayers. You can pray for yourself, your family, your church, and people who do not yet know Jesus. Your prayers will be saved on your device so you can come back to them each day.

blocks.title: Build Your Daily Prayers
blocks.description: Use the Lord's Prayer as a pattern to create your own personalized daily prayers. Add the people and needs that are on your heart right now.

blocks.text: Each day this week, pray through your six steps once, even if it only takes five minutes. Use your own words, and start with "Father." If you forget a day or your mind wanders, do not quit. Your Father is not keeping score. Just begin again.
Lesson 3 Review

Prayer is a child talking with a Father who loves to listen. Jesus gave His disciples, and you, a pattern that touches every part of life: connect with your Father, worship His name, pray His agenda first, depend on Him, forgive and be forgiven, and stand against the enemy. Use the Daily Prayers tool to start putting that pattern into practice this week.
In the next lesson, you will learn how God speaks to you through the Bible.

blocks.heading: Introduction to John 7, 8, and 9
blocks.intro: In John 7-9, Jesus continues to challenge what people think they know about God and about who He is. You will see Him defend a woman caught in her worst moment and restore sight to a man who had never seen. Pay attention to what these moments reveal about the character of Jesus.

blocks.text: Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson, and what next step can you take this week?
What have you learned about God and yourself recently in your Daily Devotions?
What is a prayer request for this week?
